t: You're at Abney Park Cemetery in Hackney, one of London's Magnificent Seven cemeteries. The best-known burials here belong to the Salvation Army. William Booth, the Methodist preacher, founded it with his wife Catherine and became its first General. Catherine, known as the Mother of the Salvation Army, is buried here too. Others lie nearby in the cemetery as well. Betsi Cadwaladr, the Welsh nurse who served in the Crimean War alongside Florence Nightingale, is one. Mary Hays, an early feminist writer close to Mary Wollstonecraft, is another. So is Walter Henry Medhurst, an early translator of the Bible into Chinese.
